title: DRDO to lead thematic session on ‘Semiconductors & Next-Gen Chips’ at ESTIC-2026
excerpt: 13 October 2026: Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) will spearhead a thematic session on ‘Semiconductors and Next-Gen Chips’ during Emerging Science, Technology & Innovation Conclave (ESTIC-2026) scheduled to be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi from October 27 to 29, 2026. The conclave is being jointly organised by 12 ministries/departments under the guidance of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India. It is a significant national initiative aimed at advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 and strengthening Aatmanirbharta through science, technology and innovation. The DRDO session will bring together eminent leaders from the industry, academia, indigenous chip-development ecosystem and defence electronics. It will feature a keynote address by VP & MD, Micron India followed by talks by CEO, Bharat Semi, CEO, Netrasemi and Director, IIT Madras. The talks will explore key developments in semiconductor technologies, purpose-built AI system-on-chips, intelligence at the silicon edge and the evolving microprocessor landscape. The speakers with diverse expertise will enable a substantive dialogue on semiconductor fabrication, chip design, AI computing, indigenous semiconductor platforms, research and development, and strategic and defence applications. The session is expected to foster stronger collaboration among industry, academia and strategic stakeholders, identify emerging technological opportunities and contribute to the development of a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, with emphasis on indigenous capabilities for critical and next-generation applications. The Outreach Stall at ESTIC 2026 will provide a platform to showcase the Ministry’s key initiatives, achievements, research programmes, and contributions to science, technology, and innovation. The stall will feature a diverse range of indigenous technologies developed by DRDO laboratories, including advanced communication systems, quantum technology prototypes, extreme-cold-weather clothing, the PRABALA female full-body protector, passive and powered exoskeletons, portable hybrid energy management systems, high-power pulse laser diodes, and scramjet engine technology. The exhibits will highlight ongoing efforts to strengthen indigenous R&D, promote technology development and self-reliance, and address critical requirements in defence and other strategic sectors. The stall will also foster collaboration among academia, industry, start-ups, and research institutions while enhancing public awareness of the Ministry’s role in advancing India’s scientific and technological capabilities. Presiding over the curtain-raiser event organised by DRDO in Bengaluru, Karnataka on October 13, 2026, Distinguished Scientist and Director General (Electronics and Communication Systems) Dr BK Das underscored the importance of semiconductors and next-gen chips for economic competitiveness, digital sovereignty and national security. He stressed that building an end-to-end, resilient microelectronics ecosystem is essential to powering telecommunications, automotive systems, industrial automation, AI hardware and strategic defence platforms as India advances towards Viksit Bharat. Dr Das added that strengthening domestic capabilities is critical to protecting the national economy from global supply-chain disruptions, geopolitical volatility and international technology export controls. He underlined India's aim to emerge as a global semiconductor powerhouse, advancing strategic autonomy and high-value exports across the microelectronics value chain. Distinguished Scientist and Director General (Technology Management) Dr Anupam Sharma highlighted the critical role of semiconductors in modern warfare, stating that these technologies are integral to virtually every aspect of military operations. He added that business in the semiconductor-related segment is expected to rise to 200 billion dollars by 2035. Director, Directorate of Extramural Research & Intellectual Property Rights, Director, Solid State Physics Laboratory, Director, Electronics and Radar Development Establishment and Center Head, Combat Aircraft Systems Development & Integration Centre were among those present on the occasion.

title: Dr Neha Agarwal: From law professor to award-winning Telangana DSP
excerpt: HYDERABAD: From law and academia to agriculture and business, the 112 probationary officers who completed their training on Monday brought diverse experiences to their new roles in policing. Among them was Dr Neha Agarwal, who won four awards at the Police Academy. She had earlier won gold medals in LLB at Osmania University and LLM […]HYDERABAD: From law and academia to agriculture and business, the 112 probationary officers who completed their training on Monday brought diverse experiences to their new roles in policing. Among them was Dr Neha Agarwal, who won four awards at the Police Academy. She had earlier won gold medals in LLB at Osmania University and LLM at Nalsar University of Law. She was also the topper of her PhD batch in law, as reported by DC. Former law academic Neha Agarwal joins students she mentored Agarwal previously worked as an assistant professor of law at Nalsar University of Law, Hyderabad, a senior law researcher at Osmania University and a senior teaching consultant for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Civil Services Examination. “Of the students I mentored, 21 were selected in the recently announced Group-I selections, including five probationary deputy superintendents of police (DSPs). I then helped my students prepare for competitive examinations. Now, the selected candidates are my batchmates,” Neha told the Media. The oldest woman probationer in the batch, Agarwal said she did not feel disadvantaged by her age or gender. She said her academic background and professional experience would help her understand women's issues and enforce the law. “I have all this experience now. Being a woman, I can listen closely to women's issues. I have studied law, and when I am posted in a city or district, I can enforce it factually. My gold medals are not going to go to waste,” she said. After the passing-out ceremony, Agarwal hugged her mother, brother and sister-in-law. She credited her family for standing by her. Probationers focus on cybercrime, drugs and artificial intelligence Shailesh Puna, 27, from Medak, sees the next phase of training as an opportunity to prepare for emerging crime trends. A graduate in political science and international relations, he wants to specialise in the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and artificial intelligence (AI). “We can see how the world is increasingly depending on AI, and I want to develop expertise in it by the time I take up a posting,” Puna said. Malkajgiri Special Branch assistant commissioner of police Ravinder Reddy watched as his son, Shantan Reddy, passed out of the academy. “My interests are cybercrime and drugs. I have seen conventional methods of crime, but the crimes of the future will increasingly involve cybercrime and drugs. I want to excel in these areas while focusing on the next six months of training,” Shantan said. He had reached the UPSC Main Examination stage twice before appearing for the DSP selection process. He had also performed field duties during Ganesh immersion in Golconda. Families celebrate officers’ achievement after training S. Rani of Mothinagar was seen kissing her daughter after the ceremony. Her daughter had stayed at the academy during the training period. Rani's husband joked that she had left their daughter's responsibilities to him. However, he said he was proud of his wife for clearing the competitive selection process. Seeing her in uniform was particularly meaningful to him. For Nanavath Dasarath, 25, becoming an officer was a moment of pride for his community. His mother, Rajamma, said the family depended on agriculture in Devarakonda and that she had ensured her son spent his time studying rather than working in the fields. “He was always interested in studying. Seeing him become an officer makes me proud. It is a moment of pride for our community,” she said. Anand urges officers to uphold constitutional values Addressing the probationers, Anand said they had completed 44 weeks of training in law, investigation, professional skills, field experience, drill, parade and sports. They will undergo another 46 weeks of practical training at the district level, he added. Anand urged the officers to remain loyal to the Constitution and serve people honestly, fearlessly and without prejudice. Police personnel must protect lives and property, preserve the dignity of the uniform and lead their teams by example, he said. He highlighted changing policing challenges, including drugs, cybercrime, organised crime, traffic congestion, road safety and food adulteration. DGP challenges officers to maintain fitness throughout careers Academy director Abhilasha Bisht urged the officers to discharge their duties with integrity and commitment. In a message on physical fitness, Anand challenged the officers to maintain their fitness throughout their careers. He said the belt buckle they wore at the passing-out parade should fit the same hole when they retired, 30 years later. ]]>

title: Gujarat Police bets on AI to save officers’ time, sharpen crime detection
excerpt: Gandhinagar, Oct 13 (IANS) Gujarat Police is looking to use artificial intelligence (AI) and software integration to reduce the time officers spend on routine tasks and improve policing, Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said at the conclusion of the 'Gujarat Police Innovation Challenge 2026' in Ahmedabad. Addressing the closing ceremony of the two-day Sentinel Hackathon 2026 at i-Hub, Sanghavi said the initiative is not limited to crime detection or the creation of technology infrastructure but also aimed to save the working hours, or ‘human hours’, of thousands of police constables and officers, allowing them to improve their social lives and spend more time with their families. More than 3,100 registrations and over 1,000 innovative solutions were received for the challenge, which brought together innovators, start-ups, technology companies and researchers from across the country to develop solutions for public safety using AI and CCTV integration. “This innovation challenge is not merely about creating IT or technology infrastructure or detecting crime. It is also a deeply human approach aimed at saving the working hours of thousands of Gujarat Police constables and officers through AI and modern software integration,” Sanghavi said. Custom Ad: Multiplex He said the effective use of software and AI could help ensure smart policing, adding that young innovators and start-ups developing CCTV integration and AI-based solutions could find business opportunities in Gujarat and other states. "The police department is committed to supporting innovators from concept development to execution and facilitating access to real-time data," he said. During the hackathon, participants demonstrated solutions using live CCTV feeds, including real-time automatic number plate recognition, vehicle tracking and watchlist matching. The competition's Phase 1 concluded with winning teams across three categories and recipients of incentive prizes being awarded a total of Rs 18 lakh. The total prize money available across Phases 1 and 2 is Rs 51 lakh. Director General of Police (DGP) G.S. Malik said integrating the state's CCTV network with AI and video analytics could help prevent crimes, identify suspicious individuals promptly and generate real-time alerts. "The solutions developed through the hackathon could strengthen proactive policing," he added. Sanjiv Kumar, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister and Principal Secretary of the Home Department, said the initiative sought to bring CCTV cameras installed by different state departments onto a single platform, allowing better use of available data and more effective outcomes.
